links.outcome: Reader sensitivity and specificity with vs without concurrent AI support; overreliance on erroneous AI
links.effect: Recall sensitivity fell from 81% (307/379) to 75% (284/379) with AI; specificity rose from 67% to 86%; net 23 fewer cancers detected; readers changed positive to negative in 21-41% of exams.
links.quote: When using AI, 39 of the cancers detected by study radiologists without AI were missed, and 16 cancers previously missed were detected with AI, resulting in a net decrease of 23 cancers detected when using AI decision support.

links.outcome: Whether radiologists detect and resist incorrect AI outputs (automation bias)
links.effect: Radiologists changed assessment from positive to negative in 21 to 41% of exams even though this was incorrect in 31 to 38% of cases.
links.quote: In our study, radiologists changed their assessment from positive to negative in 21 to 41% of the exams even though this was incorrect in 31 to 38% of cases.

links.outcome: Reader performance with AI in workflow versus standalone AI metrics
links.effect: With AI, reader sensitivity shifted toward AI operating point: sensitivity 75% vs 81% without AI, specificity 86% vs 67%; reading time fell 38%.
links.quote: The shift in study radiologist operating point caused by concurrent AI decision support demonstrates automation bias which is in line with the results of two recent publications [ 8 , 9 ].

links.outcome: Change in combined human-AI performance and reliance after AI deployment
links.effect: Radiologist operating point nudged toward AI's; authors call for careful monitoring of radiologist performance overall and individually in real-world AI implementation.
links.quote: These interaction effects may not be possible to estimate beforehand, calling for careful monitoring of radiologist performance, overall and individually, in real-world implementations of AI for screening mammography.

links.outcome: Reader performance in cancer-enriched test set versus original non-enriched screening
links.effect: Reader sensitivity was 81% without AI vs 61% originally, and specificity 67% vs 98%, showing performance in an enriched set is unrepresentative of the intended population.
links.quote: Compared to the original setting sensitivity of 61% (232/379), the reader study sensitivity was higher at 81% (307/379) without AI, which decreased to 75% (284/379) with AI decision support, a relative decrease of 7% ( p < 0.001).
